2026_011_m042126bdmtg.paragraph: Regular meeting minutes of the Troy Board of Education for Tuesday, April 21, 2026, held at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, with President Anne and Board members Alic, Haupt, Melton, Philippart, Potts and Zendler present and approximately 75 people in the audience. The Board recognized the 2026 Outstanding Teachers of the Year, adopted an Autism Acceptance Month resolution, and approved a consent agenda covering items A through M. Its most consequential action was awarding the bid for a complete renovation of Boulan Park Middle School in the amount of $7,293,050.00 as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund.
2026_011_m042126bdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, April 21, 2026, Service Center, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; adjournment at 8:35 p.m. Minutes submitted by Matt Haupt, Secretary (MH/jh).

**Attendance**
Board: Anne (President), Alic, Haupt, Melton, Philippart, Potts, Zendler. Administration: Superintendent Machesky, plus DiPilato, Griffor, Smotherman, Brennan, Griffin, Algeier, Montante, Pagel and Trudel. Approximately 75 members of the audience.

**Recognitions**
More than 49 Troy School District educators were nominated for Outstanding Teacher of the Year; three were selected. Winners: Lindsey Maliepaard, Elementary Teacher of the Year, Costello Elementary School; Tammy Gilbert, Middle School Teacher of the Year, Boulan Park Middle School; Christina Rick, Troy High School, High School and Overall Teacher of the Year. Christina Rick was also named the 2026 Oakland County High School Teacher of the Year. A reception for all nominees was set for Wednesday, April 29 at Troy High School.

A TSD Mission Moment covered the Shamrock Shakedown, a basketball tradition of Troy Center for Transition partnered with International Academy East. Teachers Brynn Lawrence (TCT) and Mark Chrzanowski (IA East) presented with students Ava Pittman (IA-East) and Nathan Kohnert (TCT).

**Autism Acceptance Month resolution**
Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Mrs. Alic. Recitals note that Autism Spectrum Disorder affects more than five million people in the United States and that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention report 1 in 36 children may have autism. The resolution recognizes April 2026 as Autism Acceptance Month in the Troy School District. Yes: 7, No: 0. A five minute recess followed.

**Consent agenda (items A through M)**
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic; Yes: 7, No: 0. Items: minutes of the March 3, 2026 Workshop; March 7, 2026 Winter Retreat; March 17, 2026 Special Meeting; March 17, 2026 Closed Session; March 17, 2026 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report for February 2026; Second Reading and Adoption of New/Revised Board Policies; E-Rate Voluntary Alternate 2; World Language Purchase (Spanish, French and German); Geometry Materials Purchase; SEAB Video (Elementary); Code of Conduct; Athletics Handbook.

**Business actions**

| Item | Mover / Support | Amount | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Boulan Park Renovation Project (Rec 2 of 3) | Alic / Potts | $7,293,050.00 | Capital Projects Fund |
| e-Rate bid pack (THS, Barnard, Bemis, Baker) | Philippart / Potts | $669,138.36 | Capital Projects Fund |
| Troy High, Baker, Barnard, Bemis renovations | Philippart / Haupt | $441,960.61 | Building Site & Sinking Fund |

All three carried Yes: 7, No: 0. Attached award schedules list Total Category Awards of $6,630,046.00 plus a 10% contingency of $663,004.00 for Boulan Park, and for the Troy High/Baker/Barnard/Bemis pack, LMS Construction at $271,997.00, Gardiner Vose, Inc. at $137,225.79 and an 8% contingency of $32,737.82.

**Other**
Personnel, Curriculum, Other and Additions/Deletions: none. One community member addressed the Board on agenda items and three on non-agenda items; no action taken. Student representatives reporting: Chloe Gentilini (Troy College and Career High School), Ahyoung Song (International Academy-East), Sara Graunstadt (Athens High School), Bella Doss (Troy High School). Board comments covered Troy Youth Assistance needing a Treasurer, a MASB Award of Distinction, the countywide enhancement millage, the TFEE Golf Outing on June 9th, the tabled Invest in My Kids ballot, CAP Day with 100 students, the IA-East Art Fair Reception and Love of Reading event on March 24, the third of five SFEG meetings, middle school math surveys, and budget discussion at the Board Retreat. Next workshop: Tuesday, April 28th; next regular meeting: Tuesday, May 19th.
2026_011_m042126bdmtg.verbose:
**Identification and attendance**
Regular meeting minutes of the Troy Board of Education, Tuesday, April 21, 2026, held at the Troy School District Services Building (Service Center), 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mrs. Anne, Board members Alic, Haupt, Melton, Philippart, Potts and Zendler were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Smotherman, Brennan, Griffin, Algeier, Montante, Pagel and Trudel. Approximately 75 members of the audience attended. The Pledge of Allegiance opened the proceedings. The meeting was adjourned at 8:35 p.m. Minutes were respectfully submitted by Matt Haupt, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typing reference MH/jh.

**Recognition: Outstanding Teachers of the Year**
The Board recognized the district's 2026 Outstanding Teachers of the Year. More than 49 Troy School District educators were nominated for the distinguished recognition, and from that group three educators were selected on the basis of passion, dedication, impact and excellence in teaching. A short video was shown capturing the administrative team surprising each winner in the classroom. A special reception for all nominees and winners was scheduled for Wednesday, April 29 at Troy High School, giving teachers an opportunity to connect with those who nominated them; each nominee was to receive a certificate, their nomination materials, and a small token of appreciation. Each of the three winners came to the podium as their name was called, shared remarks, and posed for a photo with members of the Board of Education.

The 2026 Outstanding Teachers of the Year are Lindsey Maliepaard, Elementary Teacher of the Year, Costello Elementary School; Tammy Gilbert, Middle School Teacher of the Year, Boulan Park Middle School; and Christina Rick, Troy High School, High School and Overall Teacher of the Year. All three winners were submitted to Oakland Schools to represent Troy in the countywide Outstanding Teacher Award program, and Christina Rick was named the 2026 Oakland County High School Teacher of the Year.

**TSD Mission Moment: Shamrock Shakedown**
The Mission Moment described the Shamrock Shakedown, which began as a shared passion for basketball between students and staff at Troy Center for Transition and grew into a school-wide tradition celebrating teamwork, inclusion and community. International Academy East (IA East) has been an essential partner, leading game-day setup and serving as master of ceremonies, with a soundtrack and halftime performances. Troy Center for Transition teacher Brynn Lawrence and International Academy East teacher Mark Chrzanowski were invited to the podium to introduce their students and describe the event. Ava Pittman from IA-East and Nathan Kohnert from TCT spoke about participating and shared a brief video.

**Autism Acceptance Month resolution**
April was designated Autism Acceptance Month. The resolution was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Alic. Its recitals state that Autism Spectrum Disorder affects more than five million people in the United States; that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention report that 1 in 36 children may have autism; that autism is a neurological and developmental disorder characterized by social impairment and restricted interactive and communication behaviors that can affect anyone regardless of race, ethnicity, gender or socioeconomic background; that symptoms may present in a variety of combinations and can result in significant, lifelong challenges affecting learning, daily living, employment, social-interactive behaviors, and understanding verbal and nonverbal communications; that physicians, psychologists, behavior analysts, speech and language pathologists, occupational therapists, vocational rehabilitation professionals and educators can assist persons with autism and their families through early identification, education, intervention and recreation; and that the Troy School District is committed to fostering acceptance and belonging. The resolution recognizes April 2026 as Autism Acceptance Month in the Troy School District. The vote was Yes: 7, No: 0. A five minute recess followed. There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

**Public communication**
One community member addressed the Board during public communication on agenda items; no action was taken. Three community members addressed the Board during public communication on non-agenda items; no action was taken.

**General: consent agenda**
Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic, the Board approved items A through M on the consent agenda: minutes of the March 3, 2026 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the March 7, 2026 Board of Education Winter Retreat; minutes of the March 17, 2026 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the March 17, 2026 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the March 17, 2026 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report for February 2026; Second Reading and Adoption of New/Revised Board Policies; E-Rate Voluntary Alternate 2; World Language Purchase for Spanish, French and German; Geometry Materials Purchase; SEAB Video for Elementary; Code of Conduct; and Athletics Handbook. Vote: Yes: 7, No: 0. There were no Personnel items and no Curriculum items.

**Business: Boulan Park Renovation Project (Rec 2 of 3)**
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Potts, the Board resolved that the bid for a complete renovation of Boulan Park Middle School, including architectural, mechanical, electrical and structural work, be awarded as attached in the amount of $7,293,050.00, approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes: 7, No: 0. The attached award schedule lists the following category awards:

**Business: e-Rate bid pack**
Under the heading THS, Barnard, Bemis, Baker Renovation Projects, and moved by Dr. Philippart with support from Mrs. Potts, the Board resolved that the bid for the e-Rate bid pack be awarded as attached in the amount of $669,138.36, approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. The same motion text also states that the renovation of Boulan Park Middle School be awarded to the vendors listed. Vote: Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Business: Troy High, Baker, Barnard and Bemis renovation projects**
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Haupt, the Board resolved that the bid for the Troy High, Baker, Barnard and Bemis renovation projects be awarded as listed and that $441,960.61 be approved as an expenditure of the Building Site & Sinking Fund. Vote: Yes: 7, No: 0. The attached schedule lists General Construction to LMS Construction (base bid includes Alt. 1) at $271,997.00; Operable Partition to Gardiner Vose, Inc. (including Alt. 1) at $137,225.79; Contingency 8% at $32,737.82; and TOTAL PROJECT AWARD COST of $441,960.61.

**Reports from high school student representatives**
Chloe Gentilini, student representative for Troy College and Career High School; Ahyoung Song, student representative for International Academy-East; Sara Graunstadt, student representative for Athens High School; and Bella Doss, student representative for Troy High School, each reported on events and activities at their schools.

**Board comments**
Items raised included: Troy Youth Assistance needs a Treasurer; the TSD Board received a MASB Award of Distinction; the countywide enhancement millage; the TFEE Golf Outing on June 9th in need of golfers and sponsors, with information on the website; the Invest in My Kids ballot tabled pending more signatures; Les Miserables coming soon with tickets on sale; the end of the Ramadan season with wishes for Eid and Easter; CAP Day with 100 students participating; the IA-East Art Fair Reception on March 24 at 5:00 pm; the Love of Reading event on March 24 at 5:30 pm at Athens; the third of five SFEG meetings held, with a podcast of each meeting available on the website; congratulations to Teachers of the Year Lindsey Maliepaard, Tammy Gilbert and Christina Rick; surveys distributed to parents, students and teachers regarding middle school math; and budget discussion at the Board Retreat with all options under consideration.

**Upcoming meetings**
The next Board Workshop was set for Tuesday, April 28th at the Services Building, and the next regular meeting for Tuesday, May 19th. There were no items under Other.

2026_012_m040726spbdmtg.paragraph: Special meeting minutes of the Troy Board of Education for Tuesday, April 7, 2026 at the Service Center, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, running from 6:03 p.m. to 6:22 p.m. with all seven trustees present and no one in the audience. The Board authorized a Sidewalk Easement and Highway Easement to the Board of County Road Commissioners of the County of Oakland for the new Smith Middle School, then declared it necessary to acquire permanent highway and sidewalk easements along Livernois Road and authorized Clark Hill PLC to initiate condemnation proceedings against the owners of 5836 Livernois Road, Tax Parcel No. 20-10-101-033, after negotiations failed.
2026_012_m040726spbdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education special meeting, Tuesday, April 7, 2026, Service Center, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, held at the Troy School District Services Building. President Anne called the special meeting to order at 6:03 p.m.; adjournment at 6:22 p.m. Minutes submitted by Matt Haupt, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (MH/jh).

**Attendance**
Board: Anne (President), Alic, Haupt, Melton, Philippart, Potts, Zendler. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Griffor, Pagel, DiPilato and Trudel. There was no one in the audience. The Pledge of Allegiance was recited. Public communication: none.

**Business Services, item a: Easement Agreement**
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt. The resolution recites that Troy School District desires to grant a Sidewalk Easement and a Highway Easement to the Board of County Road Commissioners of the County of Oakland in order to construct, install, operate, use, maintain, repair, replace and remove a sidewalk and roadway for the new Smith Middle School on each Property. The Board authorized both easements on terms substantially similar to the attached documents (Exhibit A) and authorized the Superintendent, or his designee, to execute them and any necessary and incidental documents. A certification clause states the resolution was duly adopted at a special meeting held on the 7th day of April, 2026, with notice given in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Vote: Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Business Services, item b: Declaration of necessity and condemnation authorization**
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Alic. The Board declared it necessary to acquire permanent highway easements and sidewalk easements along Livernois Road for the new Smith Middle School project, noting that negotiations with the Owner had not been successful and that the District has power to acquire interests in real property by condemnation under the Uniform Condemnation Procedures Act.

Key elements of the resolution:
- Project: construction and operation of the new Smith Middle School on Livernois Road, City of Troy, Oakland County, including driveway approaches and a deceleration lane on the east side of Livernois Road, road widening, traffic signal and sidewalk improvements (the Livernois Road Improvements).
- Property: owned in fee by Mirza Azam-Ali Baig and Juveria Baig, husband and wife; commonly known as 5836 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan; Tax Parcel No. 20-10-101-033.
- Authority cited: Section 11a of Michigan Public Act 451, Public Acts of 1976 (The Revised School Code), MCL 380.11a; Uniform Condemnation Procedures Act, Public Act 87 of 1980, MCL 213.51 et seq.
- Authorizations: the Superintendent, or in his absence the Deputy Superintendent of Business Affairs, may execute documents, record the Statement of Necessity and Declaration of Taking of Private Property, retain appraisers, make good faith written offers, negotiate just compensation, and initiate proceedings in the Oakland County Circuit Court.
- The Deputy Superintendent of Schools of Business Affairs is authorized to establish an escrow account with First American Title Company for amounts estimated to be just compensation, and to select a real estate appraiser or other consultants.
- Clark Hill PLC, or another firm selected by the Superintendent in the event of conflict, is retained to initiate condemnation proceedings.
- The Board reserves the right to bring federal or state cost recovery actions against the Owner for costs from any release of hazardous or toxic substances on the Easement.

**Other: workshop rescheduling**
Moved by Mrs. Zendler and supported by Mrs. Potts, the Board took action to reschedule the May 5, 2026 Board of Education Workshop to the preceding week, April 28, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. No vote tally is recorded in the minutes for this item or for item b.

**Identification and attendance**
Special board meeting minutes of the Troy Board of Education for Tuesday, April 7, 2026, held at the Troy School District Services Building (Service Center), 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. President Anne called the special meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. In addition to Mrs. Anne, Board members Alic, Haupt, Melton, Philippart, Potts and Zendler were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Griffor, Pagel, DiPilato and Trudel. There was no one in the audience. The Pledge of Allegiance was recited and there was no public communication. The meeting was adjourned at 6:22 p.m. Minutes were respectfully submitted by Matt Haupt, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, reference MH/jh.

**Business Services, item a: Easement Agreement**
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt, the Board resolved to authorize the Sidewalk Easement and Highway Easement and to authorize the Superintendent of the School District, or his designee, to execute the Sidewalk Easement and Highway Easement as well as any and all documents necessary and incidental on behalf of the School District.

The recitals state that the Troy School District desires to grant a Sidewalk Easement and a Highway Easement to the Board of County Road Commissioners of the County of Oakland in order to construct, install, operate, use, maintain, repair, replace and remove a sidewalk and roadway for the new Smith Middle School on each Property (collectively the Properties), in accordance with the terms of the Sidewalk Easement and the Highway Easement; and that the School District desires to authorize the Superintendent, or his designee, to execute those easements on terms substantially similar to those in the attached documents, which are attached and incorporated by reference as Exhibit A.

The operative provisions are: (1) the School District authorizes the Sidewalk Easement and Highway Easement on terms substantially similar to those contained in the attached instruments; and (2) the Superintendent of the School District, or his designee, is authorized to execute the Sidewalk Easement and Highway Easement as well as any and all documents necessary and incidental on behalf of the School District.

A certification block headed RESOLUTION DECLARED ADOPTED follows, certifying that the foregoing is a true and complete copy of a resolution duly adopted by the Board of Education of Troy School District, County of Oakland, Michigan, at a special meeting held on the 7th day of April, 2026, and that the meeting was conducted and public notice given pursuant to and in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, being Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, and that minutes were kept and will be or have been made available as required by that Act. The certification is signed by the Secretary, Board of Education. The recorded vote is Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Business Services, item b: Declaring necessity to acquire highway and sidewalk easement and authorizing legal counsel to initiate condemnation proceedings for the Smith Middle School project**
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Alic. The resolution states that negotiations with the Owner to acquire the easements have not been successful; that the District has power to acquire interests in real property by condemnation pursuant to the Uniform Condemnation Procedures Act; and that the Board finds it necessary to acquire permanent highway easements and sidewalk easements along Livernois Road.

The recitals identify the Troy School District as a Michigan general powers school district acting by and through its Board of Education, currently undertaking a project for construction and operation of the new Smith Middle School (the Project) located on Livernois Road in the City of Troy, Oakland County, Michigan, which includes roadway and sidewalk improvements necessary for the benefit of the public and to improve road conditions, safety, mobility and accessibility to the school and for road users. As part of the Project it is necessary to construct driveway approaches and a deceleration lane on the east side of Livernois Road, including widening the road and making traffic signal and sidewalk improvements, collectively the Livernois Road Improvements.

To undertake the Project the District must acquire permanent highway and sidewalk easements on, over, across and under certain real property owned in fee by Mirza Azam-Ali Baig and Juveria Baig, husband and wife (the Owner), situated in the City of Troy, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, commonly known as 5836 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan, Tax Parcel No. 20-10-101-033. The Easements are set forth in the Declaration of Necessity and Taking of Property attached in substantial form as Exhibit A.

Statutory authority cited includes Section 11a of Michigan Public Act 451, Public Acts of 1976 (The Revised School Code), as amended, MCL 380.11a, under which the District has power to acquire interests in real property by condemnation, and the Uniform Condemnation Procedures Act, Public Act 87 of 1980, as amended, MCL 213.51 et seq. (the UCPA), which establishes procedures for the taking of property by eminent domain. The District reserves the right to bring federal or state cost recovery actions against the Owner for costs incurred as a result of the release of hazardous or toxic substances or materials that may have occurred on the Easement. The District will present the Owner a good faith written offer to acquire the Easement in exchange for payment of just compensation based on an appraisal by a state certified appraiser; if the Owner rejects that offer, the Clark Hill PLC law firm is authorized to institute a condemnation lawsuit for acquisition of the Easements, and the Superintendent of Schools or the Deputy Superintendent of Schools of Business Affairs is authorized to execute any documents needed for the condemnation lawsuit.

The operative provisions are numbered 1 through 6. (1) The Board declares that the Project is a public improvement and that acquiring the Easements in, on, over, under, across and through the Property for the Livernois Road Improvements is necessary and essential, since those improvements benefit the public and improve public safety. (2) The Board authorizes the Superintendent of Schools, or in his absence the Deputy Superintendent of Business Affairs, to take all action and execute documents necessary under the Revised School Code, the UCPA and any other applicable state or federal law, including acquiring the Easements, recording the Statement of Necessity and Declaration of Taking of Private Property in substantial form as set forth in Exhibit A, retaining qualified appraisers or other consultants to determine just compensation, making good faith written offers to property owners, entering negotiations, reaching agreements as to just compensation, presenting good faith offers to Owners and interested parties, and initiating appropriate proceedings in the Oakland County Circuit Court for condemnation of the Easements set forth in Exhibit A. (3) The Deputy Superintendent of Schools of Business Affairs is authorized to establish an escrow account with First American Title Company for the specific amounts estimated to be just compensation for the Easements to be condemned pursuant to the UCPA. (4) Clark Hill PLC, or in the event of conflict such other firm as the Superintendent may select, is retained to take all appropriate action regarding initiation of condemnation proceedings in the Oakland County Circuit Court for the taking of private property as indicated in Exhibit A. (5) The Deputy Superintendent of Schools of Business Affairs is authorized to select a real estate appraiser or other consultants, considering estimated appraisal cost, timing of services, professional services and expert witness qualifications, to prepare estimates of just compensation required for the Easement taken as described in Exhibit A. (6) The Board of Education for the Troy School District reserves the right to bring federal or state cost recovery actions against the Owner for costs incurred as a result of the release of hazardous or toxic substances or materials that may have occurred on the Easement.

**Other: rescheduling of the Board Workshop**
Moved by Mrs. Zendler and supported by Mrs. Potts, the Board resolved to reschedule the May 5, 2026 Board of Education Workshop to the preceding week, April 28, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. No separate vote tally is printed in the minutes for this item or for Business Services item b; the only recorded tally in the minutes is Yes: 7, No: 0 on the Easement Agreement.
